paper.abstract_en: The excited states of <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Ag</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>107</mn></mmultiscripts></math> were populated via <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>Mo</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>100</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>(</mo><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>11</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>,</mo><mspace width="0.28em"/><mn>4</mn><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> reaction at the BARC-TIFR Pelletron Linac Facility located at TIFR Mumbai. The mean-life of <math><mrow><mn>15</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></math> state at 2299-keV energy level was measured using the fast timing method. The <math><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>E</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> transition strengths of 1307- and 498-keV <math><mi>γ</mi></math> rays using the measured mean-life were found to be <math><mrow><mn>4.8</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> and <math><mrow><mn>1.7</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></msup><mspace width="0.28em"/><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">W</mi><mo>.</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi><mo>.</mo></mrow></mrow></math>, respectively, indicating highly hindered transitions. The shell-model analysis was performed to understand the microscopic origin of this extremely slow <math><mrow><mi>E</mi><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> transition using both proton and neutron core excitations. This study highlights the complicated structure of <math><mrow><mn>15</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></math> state, having small wave-function admixtures from the proton <math><mrow><mn>0</mn><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> and the neutron <math><mrow><mn>1</mn><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, and <math><mrow><mn>0</mn><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> orbitals.
